title: Shape data with collections
summary: Summarize a list of order dictionaries into a count and total.

scenario.briefing: A campus report receives orders as dictionaries. Build a summary without losing empty-input behavior.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: Initialize count and total before the loop.
Add one to count and order["total"] to total.
Return both values in a dictionary.

misconceptions.description: Special-casing empty input as an error.
misconceptions.feedback: Empty input is ordinary. A summary of zero orders should return zero count and zero total.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a comprehension mutates the source.
misconceptions.feedback: A comprehension builds a new collection. The original remains unchanged.

sections.title: Lists and dictionaries shape records
sections.body: A list keeps values in insertion order and allows duplicates. A dictionary maps unique keys to values, so a record such as an order is naturally a dictionary. A list of dictionaries is the shape most JSON APIs return, and a loop over that list processes one record at a time.

sections.title: Comprehensions build new collections
sections.body: A comprehension such as [order["total"] for order in orders] creates a new list without mutating the source. Use a comprehension when the transformation is simple and a loop when several values must be accumulated at once. Both approaches preserve the input order.

sections.title: Empty input is a valid input
sections.body: A loop over an empty list runs zero times. A summary of zero orders should return a count of zero and a total of zero, not an error. Treating empty input as exceptional adds a branch that callers must handle for an ordinary case.

steps.title: Summarize order totals
steps.prompt: Edit report.py. summarize returns a dictionary with count and total for the supplied orders.

tests.description: Two orders produce the count and total.
tests.name: summarize

hints: Start count and total before iterating.
Each order contributes one to count and order["total"] to total.
Return a dictionary with both accumulated values.
count += 1; total += order["total"]; return {"count": count, "total": total}

steps.title: Collections and empty input

statements.label: A dictionary lookup by a missing key raises KeyError.
An empty collection cannot be iterated safely.
A comprehension mutates the original list.

steps.explanation: Lists and dictionaries are runtime objects with clear behavior. Iterating an empty collection is safe and should produce a meaningful empty result.
hints: Iterating an empty list is safe; it simply yields nothing.
A comprehension builds a new list instead of mutating the source.
